title: Reconstructing a target covariate from a median: when the mean is enough and when it is not
question: When a target publication reports a skewed covariate as a median with IQR or range, how much error does reconstructing its marginal put into a target-standardized contrast, and is that error a function of the reconstructed mean alone?
answer: Under an identity link with linear effect modification, yes: the contrast error is exactly the modification coefficient times the mean error. Under a logit link, no: the mean explains only 60% of the error's variance, because the reconstruction's spread and shape also enter. With strong skew and a reported range, a normal reconstruction biased the contrast by more than 1 on the identity scale and 0.4 on the log odds ratio scale, growing with sample size; a lognormal matched to the reported quantiles kept bias below 0.1.
findings: Registered test, contrast error net of the sample floor regressed on the modification coefficient times mean error: identity link slope 1.000, R^2 1.000; logit link slope 0.246, R^2 0.597.
Normal reconstruction (Wan et al.) with strong skew and a range: bias 1.15 (identity) and 0.42 (logit) at 200 patients; 2.15 (identity) at 1000, since the range grows with n.
Quantile-matched shifted lognormal: largest bias 0.092 across all 72 scenarios.
Without skew the lognormal matcher is not free: sampling asymmetry in the reported quantiles triggers it, and its bias reached 0.08, against 0.005 for the normal reconstruction.
not_answered: One covariate with a known conditional model; estimated outcome models and multivariate marginals with dependence (CMP-15) are not covered. The lognormal matcher suits right skew only. ML-NMR integration is represented by direct integration. Two cells were run before a regressor correction and discarded unread. Peer review has not been done.
design: A known conditional model integrated over target marginals reconstructed from a sample median with IQR or range; 72 scenarios crossing link, skewness, reported summary, target size (50 to 1000) and modification strength.
estimand: Target-population marginal treatment effect (difference or log odds ratio)
methods_compared: integration over the target's own sample (floor)
